The detail_verdict_text now correctly notes N2 is absent from the verification suite entirely, removing the c3 templated-language hole. Verdict remains Self-Contradicted. holes_found.description: Carry-over from c3 hole #1: detail_evidence still uses incorrect leading-order coefficient. Current text: "N2/M2 ≈ 3e for small eccentricities, yielding e ≈ 0.063 (close to the actual e ≈ 0.0549)." The correct first-order coefficient from the Darwin-Doodson tide-generating-potential expansion is (7/2)·e, not 3·e. Re-verified numerically: Doodson Table II gives M2=0.90812, N2=0.17387 → N2/M2 = 0.19146. With e=0.0549, (7/2)·e = 0.19215 matches to <1%. With 3·e = 0.16470, gap is 14% — using 3e and observed 0.19 back-solves to e=0.0633, which is 15.4% above the known lunar value 0.0549. Calling that "close" undersells a far stronger argument (1% match vs 15% gap). Re-grep confirms exact phrase "≈ 3e" still present in git HEAD c79698c as of 2026-06-15T05:08Z. No corresponding open issue exists. NARRATE-CITE: data/wins.json:WIN-051.detail_evidence carries the wrong coefficient; cross-check with Doodson 1921 (doi:10.1098/rspa.1921.0088) Table II coefficients.
holes_found.recommendation: Same fix as c3 (still unaddressed): change "N2/M2 ≈ 3e for small eccentricities, yielding e ≈ 0.063 (close to the actual e ≈ 0.0549)" to "N2/M2 ≈ (7/2)·e at leading order (from the Darwin-Doodson expansion of the tide-generating potential for a Keplerian orbit; Doodson 1921, Table II); the observed N2/M2 ≈ 0.19 back-solves to e ≈ 0.054, matching the measured lunar eccentricity e ≈ 0.0549 to better than 1%." This converts the argument from "the dome's implied eccentricity is 15% off" to "the dome's implied eccentricity matches to 1% — but they didn't derive it," which is strictly stronger and removes a self-inflicted fact-check opening.

stronger_arguments.description: Reaffirm c3 stronger_argument: N2 is one of ~12 eccentricity/nodal sidebands in the Doodson expansion (L2, 2N2, μ2, MK3, etc.). If the dome accepts N2 as aetheric-confirmed, it must also explain the companion sidebands at the SAME order in e (L2 ≈ 0.028·M2, 2N2 ≈ 0.024·M2). kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model correctly identifies N2 as a Doodson 1921 standard tidal constituent at the correct period to one-second precision (data/wins.json:WIN-051.detail_evidence cites the canonical "12.66 hours" tabulated since Doodson 1921, via doi:10.1098/rspa.1921.0088). Including five constituents (M2, S2, K1, O1, N2) rather than only the principal two shows awareness that tidal dynamics involves multiple orbital timescales — apogee/perigee modulation, lunar declination, solar forcing — beyond a simple two-body picture. This is more sophisticated than a minimal flat-Earth model would attempt.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Awareness is not derivation. N2 is the only constituent whose amplitude ratio to the principal tide directly encodes a fundamental orbital parameter (eccentricity). Matching the tabulated 12.6583 h period is equivalent to reciting a constant from a reference table — Doodson 1921, Table II, line N2; cross-check confirmed against NOAA CO-OPS harmonic-constituent listing — and constitutes the definition of a post-hoc claim per data/wins.json:WIN-051.detail_verdict_text's own "trivial-transcription test" language. Without deriving the N2/M2 amplitude ratio (0.1915) from dome geometry, the dome has not PREDICTED N2 — it has copied the period and left the physics unresolved. raw-text/08-live-power.txt confirms there is no dome-side calculation; data/wins.json:WIN-051.detail_verdict_text's own observation that "no monitor.py entry exists for this tidal constituent at all" is the operative concession.

deeper_analysis:
Cycle 4 assessment: the c3-hole-#3 (templated live-fetch wording) has been resolved. Current detail_verdict_text now correctly notes "no monitor.py entry exists for this tidal constituent at all — the dome author has not included N2 in the verification suite — making even that weaker timestamp test inapplicable." The wording is strictly stronger than c3 and the +163-char drift is justified.

However, three c3 holes (#1 3e coefficient, #2 advocate-mode gear-motion preempt, #4 12.6580 period) remain UNADDRESSED. None has a tracked open issue in monitor/decisions/open-issues.json (re-checked: zero hits for WIN-051). The most likely cause is that c3 was written as recommendations rather than actionable findings the decider routed to ISS at the time. The c3 review itself was thorough and correctly characterized each as moderate/minor; the decider may have deferred them because hole #3 (the larger structural fix) was the priority and these three smaller fixes did not get queued behind it.

The three carry-over fixes are independent — any can be applied without the others. The 3e→(7/2)·e fix is the most impactful (it converts a "15% off" caveat into a "1% match" emphatic) and the easiest (single sentence rewrite, no new sources required). The advocate-mode preempt requires one new sentence; the period precision fix requires one digit change. Total expected edit cost: ~3 minutes of decider self-apply.

Confidence holds at 0.91 (slightly down from c3 0.93 to reflect: argument is fundamentally sound and the verdict remains correct, but three c3 fixes have aged 59 days without action — this is the second cycle flagging the same numerical error, which is itself a minor reliability signal). No verdict change. No major rewrite. "minor_edit" recommendation stands.

For the other side: a sympathetic reader could argue the carry-over holes are cosmetic (3e vs 7/2·e is a back-solve error that doesn't change the qualitative argument; 12.6580 vs 12.6583 is 1 second on a 12+ hour period; the advocate-mode preempt addresses a defense that may not arise in practice). On those grounds, the current text "works" and the c4 recommendation is over-engineering. The counter-counter: the dome author DOES read this review (per CLAUDE.md author-contact note 2026-04-27), and N2 IS the strongest tidal WIN we make. If the dome author finds a numerical sloppiness in our strongest tidal argument, it discredits the entire tidal-WINs section. The fixes are cheap enough that the cost-benefit clearly favors applying them.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A dome defender, having read our review carefully, could mount the following critique: "Even granting your N2/M2 amplitude-ratio argument, your own text contains a coefficient error (3e instead of 7/2·e) that you have flagged in two consecutive curmudgeon cycles and not fixed. If your own quantitative argument is sloppy, why should we accept your structural argument? Furthermore, you reject our claim that N2 arises from 'the lunar elliptic circuit' because we have no derivation — but your alternative explanation (Keplerian eccentricity) is itself unstated mathematically in YOUR detail_evidence (you wave at Doodson 1921 without reproducing the derivation). The asymmetry is rhetorical, not principled." This is the strongest defense and it lands because our own carry-over holes give it ammunition.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: The advocate-mode defense_survives rating is raised from c3 (3) to c4 (4) precisely because the dome author now has the c3 review's own text as ammunition — "your own debunk admits the 3e formula is wrong and you still haven't fixed it." Applying the c3 fixes (holes #1 and #4 here) defuses this defense at zero scientific cost. Once the (7/2)·e correction lands, the argument shifts from "we say your prediction is sloppy and our text is also slightly sloppy" to "we say your prediction is sloppy and we've done the derivation ourselves to 1% agreement with observation."

quantitative_verification.computations: Re-ran c3's arithmetic in Python: Doodson 1921 Table II equilibrium coefficients M2=0.90812, N2=0.17387 → N2/M2 = 0.17387/0.90812 = 0.19146. Using "N2/M2 ≈ 3e" with e=0.0549 gives 0.16470 (14.5% below observed 0.1915). Using "N2/M2 ≈ (7/2)·e" gives 0.19215 (0.4% above observed). Inverse: from N2/M2 = 0.19, the 3e formula back-solves to e = 0.0633 (15.4% above actual 0.0549); the (7/2)·e formula back-solves to e = 0.0543 (1.1% below actual). Period discrepancy: 12.6583 h − 12.6580 h = 1.08 seconds. All c3 numerical findings re-confirmed.
quantitative_verification.discrepancies: Two carry-over numerical imprecisions in the review text: (a) detail_evidence uses N2/M2 ≈ 3·e (incorrect leading-order coefficient; the correct factor is 7/2 from the Doodson tide-generating-potential expansion) — back-solved e = 0.063 is 15.4% above the known lunar value, undercutting our "close to the actual" claim; (b) detail_evidence states the period as 12.6580 h vs canonical 12.6583 h — 1.08-second cosmetic gap. Both are easily fixed and both would strengthen the argument by making it precise rather than approximate.
